title: How to change cursor in Chrome on Mac: manual steps for system and browser
metaTitle: How to change cursor in Chrome on Mac: Step by Step
description: Learn how to change cursor in Chrome on Mac using system accessibility settings or browser extensions to improve your web browsing experience today.
intro: You cannot change the cursor directly within Google Chrome settings, but you can modify it using macOS system preferences or browser extensions. This guide explains how to adjust your system pointer and how to install extensions for custom web-specific cursors.
tldr: Use System Settings to change the pointer size or color for your entire Mac.
Install a Chrome extension to use custom cursor icons while browsing the web.
Press F7 to toggle Caret Browsing if you need a text-based navigation cursor.
Remember that extensions do not work on internal Chrome pages like the Settings menu.

blocks.text: Why you cannot change the cursor in Chrome settings

Many users look for a cursor menu inside Google Chrome. You will not find one. Chrome relies on the operating system to handle pointer rendering. This keeps the browser lightweight and ensures consistent performance across different hardware. If you find instructions claiming a native setting exists, they likely refer to ChromeOS on a Chromebook, not a Mac.
How to adjust your system pointer on macOS

The most effective way to change your cursor experience is through the macOS System Settings. This change applies to every app you use, including Chrome. It is the best way to improve visibility if you struggle to track your pointer on high-resolution displays.

items: Click the Apple Menu icon in the top left corner of your screen.
Select System Settings from the drop down menu.
Navigate to Accessibility in the sidebar.
Click on Display to see your visual options.
Select Pointer to adjust your settings.

blocks.text: Once in the Pointer menu, you can drag the slider to increase the pointer size. You can also change the outline color and the fill color. These changes are immediate. If you want a more distinct cursor, choose a high-contrast color like bright yellow or neon green. You can also toggle the option to shake the mouse to find the pointer.
Using Chrome extensions for custom cursors

If you want a specific cursor icon, such as a character or a themed object, you need a browser extension. These extensions inject custom CSS into the webpages you visit. They only work when your mouse is inside the browser window.

items: Open the Chrome Web Store in your browser.
Search for Custom Cursor for Chrome.
Click the blue Add to Chrome button.
Confirm the installation by clicking Add extension in the prompt.
Click the Extensions puzzle icon in the top right toolbar.
Pin the extension for easier access.
Open the extension menu and pick a cursor pack to apply it.

blocks.text: Be aware that custom cursor extensions cannot modify internal Chrome pages. This includes the new tab page, your settings, and the Chrome Web Store itself. The cursor will revert to the default system pointer on these pages for security reasons.
blocks.title: Extension Limitations

blocks.text: Sometimes the issue is not the visual pointer, but the text cursor. If you find it hard to select text or navigate a page, try Caret Browsing. This feature places a blinking cursor on the page, allowing you to move through text with your arrow keys.

To activate this, simply press F7 on your keyboard while inside Chrome. A dialog box will appear asking if you want to turn on Caret Browsing. Select Yes. You can now highlight text by holding Shift and using your arrow keys. This is a powerful tool for users who prefer keyboard navigation over mouse clicking.

If your cursor does not change after installing an extension, try refreshing the page. Extensions often need a fresh load to apply their styles correctly. If the problem persists, check if another extension is conflicting with your cursor tool. Disabling other extensions one by one can help identify the culprit.

Accessibility is a major factor in modern web design. With nearly 300 accessibility issues identified on the average webpage, users must often take control of their own browsing experience. Customizing your cursor is one of the simplest ways to make the web more readable and usable for your specific needs.

faq.question: Can I change the cursor color in Chrome settings?
faq.answer: No, Chrome does not have a native setting for cursor colors. You must use the macOS System Settings for system-wide pointer changes or an extension for browser-specific styles.

faq.question: Why does my custom cursor disappear on some pages?
faq.answer: Browsers restrict extensions from modifying internal pages like the settings menu or the new tab page for security and stability reasons.

faq.question: Does changing the cursor affect my Mac performance?
faq.answer: Using a simple system pointer change has no impact on performance. However, some complex animated cursor extensions can consume a small amount of extra memory.

task: How to change cursor in Chrome on Mac

steps.name: Open System Settings
steps.text: Click the Apple menu and select System Settings to start changing your pointer.

steps.name: Go to Accessibility
steps.text: Find and click on the Accessibility tab in the sidebar.

steps.name: Adjust Pointer
steps.text: Click Display, then Pointer, and use the sliders to change your cursor size and color.

troubleshooting.problem: Cursor does not change after installing extension
troubleshooting.fix: Reload the web page to ensure the extension scripts run correctly.

troubleshooting.problem: Extension is not visible in Chrome
troubleshooting.fix: Click the puzzle icon in the toolbar and pin the extension to your bar.
